compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

From a `make worktree` worktree, the tracker resolves to the WORKTREE's path, not the
canonical store's — because `.tickets-tracker` there is a symlink that nothing resolves:

```
cwd               : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug
repo_root(None)   : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug
tracker_dir(None) : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug/.tickets-tracker
realpath of that  : /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker          <-- the real store
```

Every per-store sidecar in `.rebar` is then derived from `os.path.dirname(tracker)`
(`enrich_drain._rebar_dir`), so it lands in the WORKTREE's own `.rebar`, which is a real
directory and not a symlink:

```
drain lock : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug/.rebar/enrich-drain.lock
drain log  : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug/.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log
```

Three consequences, in descending severity:

**1. The drain advisory lock does not serialise drains on the shared store.** Two agents
working in two worktrees hold two DIFFERENT lock files while draining the SAME queue. The
lock's whole purpose — "an advisory lock so two drainers do not overlap"
(`enrich_drain._acquire_advisory_lock`) — is defeated exactly when it matters. This host
currently has 105 worktrees.

**2. The drain log is scattered and disposable.** A drain child spawned from a worktree logs
into that worktree's `.rebar/logs`, which is deleted with the worktree. This is why
`3198-438c-72a5-470f` recorded only four tracebacks in the canonical log for a condition that
recurs by design — most of the evidence was thrown away with the worktrees that produced it.

**3. A long-lived child can be handed a tracker path that vanishes.** The detached child gets
the unresolved worktree path as `argv[1]`, so after the worktree is retired it fails with

```
Error: cannot list '/Users/joeoakhart/split-config-writer/.tickets-tracker'
```

— which is the one symptom in that log NOT explained by the cwd bug fixed in
`3198-438c-72a5-470f`. That fix deliberately changed only the child's `cwd` and left the argv
tracker alone, because moving it would relocate the lock and the log too, which is this
ticket.

## Scope (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)

Decide where the boundary belongs, then apply it in one place — either resolve the tracker
through symlinks at the point sidecar paths are derived (`enrich_drain._rebar_dir` and its
equivalents), or resolve it at `config.tracker_dir`, which is broader and needs care because
`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` and decoupled stores also flow through it. Whichever is chosen, the
invariant to establish and test is: **one store means one drain lock and one drain log,
regardless of which worktree the write came from.**

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two writes from two different worktrees of the same store contend on the SAME drain
      advisory lock.
- [ ] A drain spawned from a worktree writes to the canonical store's drain log, and that log
      survives the worktree's removal.
- [ ] A detached child is never handed a tracker path that lives inside an ephemeral worktree.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Found while fixing `3198-438c-72a5-470f`. Same underlying theme — ephemeral worktree paths
outliving their worktree — but a different artifact (the tracker path and everything derived
from it, rather than the child's inherited cwd) and a different blast radius, so filed rather
than folded in.
compiled_state.title: worktree-local drain lock does not serialise a shared store
